transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I came in because... since my grandson was killed, something is just wrong with me. My daughter can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know in my head that I love her, but... I cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all. I just feel empty.
How long ago did your grandson pass away?
It was six days ago. He was killed right outside the community center... and this has just been going on for the six days since it happened.
When you feel this emptiness, do you also feel like you're detached from your own body or watching yourself from outside, or like the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike?

Yes, I do. It's... it's hard to explain, but sometimes I'll be sitting in my own living room, and it just looks flat and strange. Almost like I'm looking at everything through stained church glass, you know? And when I get up to do something, it feels like I'm just... watching this old woman move around. Like I'm not really inside my own body anymore.

Besides this feeling of unreality, have you noticed things like unwanted memories or images of your grandson's death popping into your mind, feeling jumpy or on edge, or having trouble sleeping since it happened?

Yes, the memories are... they're very strong. I'll just be doing something normal, like folding a quilt square or reaching for my tea, and all of a sudden I hear those shots again. I see him lying there outside the community center... just like it is happening right in front of me.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or conversations that remind you of what happened to your grandson?

Yes, I have. I absolutely will not go near that street anymore. And... I've stopped answering phone calls about the repast at the community center. I just can't talk about it. Even the music... if second-line music comes on the radio, I have to turn it off the instant I hear it, because it just pulls me straight back to that moment.

Since it happened six days ago, have these feelings of unreality, the intrusive memories, and the avoidance been present every single day without let-up, or have there been times when you felt more like your normal self again?

No, there haven't been any breaks. It's been every single day, just... constant. This has been going on for the full six days since he was killed outside the center. I haven't felt like my normal self once.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient developed severe psychological symptoms within days of witnessing/learning of her grandson's violent death (a clear, identifiable traumatic stressor). Symptoms include marked dissociative features (depersonalization—feeling detached from her own body/watching herself; derealization—environment appearing unreal, 'flat,' viewed as through stained glass), intrusive re-experiencing (vivid intrusive memories/flashbacks triggered by reminders), and avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (avoiding the street, phone calls about the repast, and evocative music). Symptoms began immediately after the trauma and have been continuous and pervasive for 6 days without remission, consistent with an acute stress reaction occurring within the first month after a traumatic event. The short duration (<1 month) and dissociative predominance distinguish this from PTSD (F43.1), which requires symptoms >1 month, and from a primary dissociative disorder (F44.81), since the dissociative symptoms here are directly and temporally linked to a discrete acute trauma rather than a longstanding dissociative pattern.
